prompt: In 120 to 180 words, analyze missing-data mechanisms in exactly five numbered points. Distinguish MCAR, MAR, and MNAR, include one failure mode, and finish with a one-sentence conclusion.

turns.assistant_message:
Missing data can occur due to three main mechanisms: Missing Completely at Random (MCAR), Missing at Random (MAR), and Missing Not at Random (MNAR). Understanding these mechanisms is crucial for handling missing data effectively in statistical analysis.

1. MCAR occurs when the likelihood of a value being missing is independent of both observed and unobserved variables. In this case, missing data do not introduce bias, as they are unrelated to any other variable in the dataset.
